description_en: Revered as one of the four main Vārāhī temples of the Kathmandu valley, Vajravārāhī is widely known as a temple without a finial. However, historical sources reveal that a golden finial was installed on the temple in 1735 CE (NS 855) in the course of a renovation.The Vajravārāhī temple, located in the Cāpāgāũ jungle south of Lalitpur, is historically referred to as "Vatābu Devala" (NS 998/1878 CE). The goddess herself is known as " Vatābu Vajravārāhī Devī" (NS 819/1699 CE). This nomenclature stems from the temple's eastward position relative to Cāpāgāũ, with "vaṃtā" being the local term for east.As one of the four cardinal Vārāhī deities of the Kathmandu valley— Nīlavārāhī in the east, Dhumavārāhī in the west, Śvetavārāhī in the north, and Vajravārāhī in the south—she is widely revered. While some Buddhists perceive her as a Ḍākinī arising from a cremation ground (Slusser 1982, p. 325), others identify her as the female energy of the Vajrayāna deity Herukacakrasamvara (B. Pradhan VS 2052, p. 1). Devotees flock to the temple, seeking blessings for healing and fulfillment of desires, making it a popular pilgrimage site.The Cāpāgāũ forest, home to the Vajravārāhī temple and abundant in medicinal herbs, is shrouded in local beliefs. It is said that fallen leaves from the forest trees are mysteriously swept away by the wind before nightfall. Monkeys exiled from the community for falling off a tree, after a brief sojourn in the forest, are surprisingly welcomed back. Crows, too, are absent from this grove (V. Karmācārya VS 2075, p. 39). Locals abstain from using the forest's wood and fallen leaves, fearing adverse consequences like nightmares and illness. An exception is made for the Bulu residents, who are permitted to use the wood for funeral pyres (temple caretaker, Dyaḥlā, female, age 58).The Vajravārāhī temple faces west and has two tiers of copper roofs but no finial. In the Kathmandu valley, only two temples lack finials: Vajravārāhī and Maru Gaṇeśa (KAT1930). There are various legends explaining why this temple doesn't have a finial. One belief is that the temple is surrounded by nine cremation grounds and a finial cannot be placed until all nine cremation grounds are used simultaneously for cremation (S. Mānandhara VS 2059, p. 23). Another belief is that the goddess herself wished for the temple to be without a finial (Slusser 1982, p. 326). Yet another legend states that during the cremation of a Cāpāgāũ resident, when the corpse was half-burnt and the skull cracked open, a devotee could offer a finial (B. Pradhāna VS 2052, p. 3).*The sanctum entrance is adorned with a metaltoraṇabearing a Vajravārāhī statue. Inside, there are statues of Vajravārāhī and other mother goddesses (mātrikā), which are later additions to the temple. The main deity, however, is not any of these statues but the waterhole (kuṇḍa) within the sanctum. Legend has it that this spot was once a dirty pond frequented by Vajravārāhī in sow form. A madman's attack on the sow led to its divine transformation and the establishment of the Vajravārāhī Pīṭha (S. Mānandhara VS 2059, p. 60). Locals believe that sprinkling water from the waterhole on damaged crops can improve their yield (V. Karmācārya VS 2075, p. 38). A buffalo statue is established in front of the temple.The exact construction date of the temple remains unknown. However, considering the prominence of Vajrayāna Buddhism in the valley between the 9th and 12th centuries, the establishment of these deities likely falls within this period (B. Pradhan VS 2052, p. 1). According to theDevamālā Vaṃśāvalī, initially, the site was a simple open shrine (pīṭha). King Śrīnivāsa Malla later constructed a grand temple and commissioned a golden statue of Vajravārāhī. This statue was ceremonially consecrated by Viśvanātha Upādhyāya on Monday, the 8th of the bright fortnight of Caitra, 1666 CE (NS 786) (Yogī Naraharinātha VS 2013, p. 58).While theBhāṣāVaṃśāvalīdoesn't explicitly mention Śrīnivāsa Malla's temple construction, it does credit him with the installation of the golden statue following its completion on the 8th of the bright fortnight of Caitra, 1666 CE (NS 786). According to this chronicle, the statue was consecrated three days later on the 11th of the same month and year, following a procession around Cāpāgāũ (D. Lamsāla VS 2023, p. 66). In 1706 CE (NS 826), a severe drought prompted Yogamatī (daughter of King Yoganarendra Malla) and King Lokaprakāśa Malla (Yogamatī's son) to perform special prayers at various temples, including Vajravārāhī, to invoke rainfall (D. Lamsāla VS 2023, p. 74).Historical records indicate the temple's existence dating back to the later medieval period. In 1699 CE (NS 819), Heranī Mayī of Cāpāgāũ donated eightropanīs of land to support the temple. King Yoganarendra Malla, in 1700 CE (NS 820), offered a stone buffalo statue with a golden parasol after performing a night-long fire sacrifice with music and offerings. King Viṣṇu Malla of Lalitpur renovated the temple in 1735 CE (NS 855), installing a golden finial, contrary to the popular belief of the temple being finial-less. Subsequent reconstructions might have led to the removal of the finial, giving rise to various legends.The temple underwent renovations in 1930 CE (VS 1987) by Jītagovinda (Yogī Naraharinātha VS 2013, p. 58) and in 1959 CE (VS 2015) by King Mahendra. In 2000 CE (VS 2057), copper sheets were added to the roof. The 2015 earthquakes caused damage to the eastern wall, which was later repaired with financial assistance of NRs. 2 million from the Department of Archaeology (V. Karmācārya VS 2075, p. 61).A Karmācārya priest oversees the daily rituals at the temple. To sustain these practices, land and a flower garden were allocated for offerings. Records from the Guthi Sansthan, a government body overseeing the management of socio-cultural trusts, indicate a land endowment of tworopanis eightānās for the daily worship of Vajravārāhī (Guṭhī Saṃsthāna VS 2071, p. 46). However, the temple currently receives no support from the Guthi Sansthan. Traditionally, musicians would play the shehnai during morning rituals and eveningāratīin the temple courtyard (V. Karmacharya VS 2075, p. 41). This practice, however, has ceased due to the loss of the allocated land.Financial constraints led to the discontinuation of daily worship for several decades. In 2023 CE (VS 2079), a week-long fire sacrifice ceremony was held to raise funds for an endowment, enabling the resumption of daily rituals. The Dyaḥlā community, comprising twelve families, takes turns in performing the temple's caretaking duties on a 15-day rotation.The palanquin procession of Vajravārāhī takes place twice a year: on the full moon day of Caitra and the 8th of the bright fortnight of Kārtika. Two distinct statues of Vajravārāhī are dedicated to these processions and are housed in the Vajravārāhī temple situated in the Bhansāra Ṭola. A stone inscription dating back to 1699 CE (NS 819) records the endowment of land for both processions, confirming their existence prior to this date.The palanquin procession on the full moon day of Caitra marks the most significant festival of Vajravārāhī. This occasion is also known as Sindūra Jātrā, as vermilion (sindūra) is sprinkled during the festivities. A legend surrounds the origin of this procession. According to one account, King Narendradeva of Bhaktapur was returning home from a war late one night, passing through Cāpāgāũ. Dispatching a soldier to seek shelter at a nearby goddess's house, the soldier returned terrified, describing a fearsome figure shrouded in white cloth. Intrigued, the king ventured forth and, upon uncovering the figure, was blessed with a vision of Goddess Vajravārāhī herself. The goddess instructed him to create a statue in her likeness and to celebrate a festival on the full moon day of Caitra. Following her divine command, a statue and palanquin were crafted, and the procession has been celebrated ever since (temple caretaker, Dyaḥlāḥ, female, age 58). An alternative legend attributes the divine encounter to King Ari Malla (S. Mānandhara VS 2059, p. 62).In 1968 CE (VS 2025), the Vajravārāhī statue used for the annual procession was stolen from its shrine (dyaḥchẽ) in Bhansāra Ṭola (V. Karmacharya VS 2075, p. 38). It was later discovered abandoned in the bushes of the Tribhuvan International Airport, likely discarded after a failed attempt to smuggle it out of the country. The government stipulated that the statue would only be returned to Cāpāgāũ if someone could guarantee its security. As no one came forward, the statue remained under the protection of the National Museum from 1972 CE (VS 2029) onwards.A replacement statue was subsequently created for the procession, but it too was stolen and has never been recovered. A third statue was then made to continue the tradition. In 2021 CE (VS 2078), the original statue was returned to Cāpāgāũ after completing the necessary legal procedures. The National Museum's director formally handed over the statue to the local trust in the presence of the mayor and deputy mayor of Godawari Municipality, representatives from the Lalitpur District Administration Office, the Department of Archaeology, and local trustees. Currently, thedyaḥchẽhouses two Vajravārāhī statues: the original, and the second replacement statue.Locals refer to the palanquin procession on the 8th of the bright fortnight of Kārtika as the " Marasti Jātrā." During this procession, a gilded head sculpture of Vajravārāhī, along with theaṣṭamātṛkādeities, is carried on a palanquin. While the Deśāra community of Cāpāgāũ currently organizes this procession, it was historically managed by the residents of Bulu, a neighboring village.Local legend has it that the residents of Bulu would bring the head sculpture of Vajravārāhī to the temple for worship before the procession began. After completing the rituals, they entrusted a young girl with the care of the goddess's sculpture while they went on a picnic. Young men from Cāpāgāũ's Deśāra caste approached the girl and tempted her with a choice: "Do you prefer the goddess or bread?" When she expressed her hunger, they offered her bread, seized control of the Vajravārāhī statue, and paraded it around the village in a procession (Pradhan 1981, p. 8). Although they lost the right to conduct the procession, Bulu residents still actively participate in the event to this day.The festival was suspended for a long time due to the theft of Vajravārāhī’s head sculpture in c. 1985-1986 CE (VS 2042-2043). In 2022 CE (VS 2079), a new statue was made, and the procession resumed (local resident, Deśāra, male, age 44).* This temple was not originally without a spire. There is an inscription (CHG0110_I_004) indicating that King Viṣṇu Malla had offered the temple a golden finial during its renovation in 1735 CE (NS 855).
description_ne: काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका चार प्रमुख वाराहीमध्ये एक मानिने वज्रवाराहीको मन्दिरलाई गजूर नभएको मन्दिर भनिएपनि नेसं ८५५ (सन् १७३५) मा राजा विष्णु मल्लले मन्दिर जीर्णोद्धार गर्दा सुनको गजूर चढाएको अभिलेखीय प्रमाण भेट्टिएको छ । प्रत्येक वर्ष चैत्र शुक्ल पूर्णिमा र कार्तिक शुक्ल ८ मा गरी वर्षको दुईपल्ट वज्रवाराहीको खटजात्रा मनाइन्छ ।ललितपुरको दक्षिणमा रहेको चापागाउँको जङ्गलमा वज्रवाराही मन्दिर रहेको छ । नेवारीमा पूर्व दिशालाई 'वंता' भनिने र चापागाउँको पूर्वपट्टिको क्षेत्रमा वज्रवाराही अवस्थित रहेकोले अभिलेखमा वज्रवाराहीलाई 'वताबु वज्रवाराहीदेवी' (नेसं ८१९) र वज्रवाराही मन्दिरलाई 'वताबु देवल' (नेसं ९९८) भनिएको पाइन्छ । काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका चार दिशामा चार वाराही स्थापना गरिएका छन् । ती चार वाराहीहरू पूर्वमा नीलवाराही, पश्चिममा धुमवाराही, उत्तरमा श्वेतवाराही र दक्षिणमा वज्रवाराही हुन् । चार मुख्य वाराहीमध्ये एकमा पर्ने हुनाले वज्रवाराहीलाई महत्त्वपूर्ण देवीको रूपमा पुजिन्छ । बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बीहरूमध्ये कोही यिनलाई मसानको बीचबाट उत्पन्न भएकी डाकिनीको रूपमा पूजा गर्छन् (Slusser 1982, p. 325) भने कोही वज्रयानी देवता हेरुकचक्रसम्वरकी स्त्री-शक्ति मान्छन् (B. Pradhāna VS 2052, p. 1) । कुनै मानिस बिरामी हुँदा यस मन्दिरमा आएर पूजा, प्रार्थना गरेपछि रोग निको हुने र मनले चिताएको इच्छा पूरा हुने विश्वासले दर्शन गर्नआउने भक्तजनको भीड लाग्ने गर्छ ।चापागाउँको पूर्वपट्टि रहेको जङ्गलमा वज्रवाराहीको मन्दिर निर्माण गरिएको छ । प्रशस्त मात्रामा जडीबुटी रहेको यस जङ्गलबारे स्थानीयहरूमा केही विश्वासहरू कायम रहेका छन् । जस्तै - जङ्गलमा रहेका रुखका पातहरू झरेपनि साँझ परेपछि रुखको फेदमा समेत नरहने गरी बतासले उडाएर लैजान्छ; रुखबाट खसेर समुदायबाट निष्कासन गरिएका बाँदरहरू यस जङ्गलमा केही दिन बसेर फर्केपछि पुन: उनीहरूले समुदायले स्वीकार्छ; यस जङ्गलमा कागले बसोबास गर्दैन (V. Karmācārya, p. 39) । यस जङ्गलका काठ, रुखबाट झरेका पात स्थानीय बासिन्दाले प्रयोग गर्नुहुँदैन, कसैले बदमाशी गरेर लगेको खण्डमा नराम्रो सपना देखेर बिरामी हुन्छ भन्ने मान्यता रहिआएको छ । बुलुका मानिस मर्दा भने अन्त्येष्टिको लागि यस जङ्गलको काठ प्रयोग गर्न छुट दिइएको छ (Dyaḥpāḥlāḥ of the temple from a Dyaḥlāḥ caste, female, age 58) ।वज्रवाराहीको मन्दिर पश्चिमाभिमुख गरी निर्माण गरिएको छ । यस मन्दिरमा दुई तह तामाको छाना राखिएका छन् तर मन्दिरमा गजूर राखिएको छैन । काठमाडौं उपत्यकामा वज्रवाराही मन्दिर र मरु गणेश मन्दिर (KAT1930) गरी दुईवटा मात्र गजूरविहीन मन्दिर रहेका छन् । यस मन्दिरमा किन गजूर राखिएन भन्ने बारे विभिन्न अनुश्रुतिहरू रहेका छन् । एकथरीको भनाइअनुसार यो मन्दिर नौवटा मसानहरूले घेरिएका छन् । ती नौवटै मसानमा एकैपल्ट मुर्दा पोल्न नल्याएसम्म मन्दिरमा गजूर राख्नु हुँदैन (S. Mānandhara VS 2059, p. 23) । देवी स्वयंको इच्छाले यो मन्दिरमा गजूर नराखिएको भन्ने भनाइ पनि रहेको छ (Slusser 1982, p. 326) । अर्को भनाइअनुसार चापागाउँ निवासी कुनै व्यक्तिको अन्त्येष्टि भइरहँदा लाश आधा जलिसकेको र आधा बाँकी रहेको अवस्थामा खप्पर पड्की गिदी निस्किरहेको अवधिभित्रमा कुनै श्रद्धालु भक्तजनले गजूर चढाउन चाहेमा चढाउन सक्छन् (B. Pradhāna VS 2052, p. 3) ।* मन्दिरको गर्भगृहभित्र प्रवेश गर्ने ढोकामाथि वज्रवाराही अङ्कित धातुको तोरण राखिएको छ । गर्भगृहभित्र वज्रवाराही लगायत मातृकाका मूर्तिहरू स्थापना गरिएका छन् । ती मूर्तिहरू मन्दिरको मुख्य मूर्ति होइनन्, पछिमात्र स्थापना गरिएका हुन् । यस मन्दिरकी प्रमुख देवी वज्रवाराहीको मूर्ति छैन, गर्भगृहभित्र रहेको कुण्डलाई नै वज्रवाराही मानी पूजा गरिन्छ । पहिले त्यस ठाउँमा फोहोर पोखरी थियो र वज्रवाराहीदेवी सुंगुर (वाराही) को रूप लिएर त्यस पोखरीमा खेल्न आउँथिन् । एकपल्ट कुनै एक बौलाहाले त्यस सुंगुरमाथि बन्चरो प्रहार गरी घाइते बनाइदिएकोले सुंगुर त्यसै ठाउँमा सिद्ध भई वज्रवाराही पीठको उत्पत्ति भएको थियो (S. Mānandhara VS 2059, p. 60) । कसैको धानखेती, तरकारी बाली नोक्सान भएमा वज्रवाराहीदेवीको गर्भगृहभित्र रहेको कुण्डको जल लगी खेतमा छरेमा बालीनाली सप्रेर उत्पादन बढ्ने विश्वास पनि रहेको छ (V. Karmācārya VS 2075, p. 38) । मन्दिरअगाडि प्राङ्गणमा राँगोको प्रतिमा स्थापना गरिएको छ ।यो मन्दिर कुन मितिमा निर्माण गरिएको भन्ने बारे कुनै अभिलेख पाइएको छैन । सम्भवतः यी देवीको स्थापना उपत्यकामा वज्रयान अधिक प्रभावशाली भएको अवधि ईशाको ९ औं देखि १२ औं शताब्दीभित्र भएको हुनुपर्छ (B. Pradhāna VS 2052, p. 1) ।देवमालावंशावलीमा उल्लेख गरिएअनुसार पहिले पीठ मात्र थियो, मन्दिर निर्माण गरिएको थिएन । राजा श्रीनिवास मल्लले अग्लो मन्दिर निर्माण गरिदिएका थिए । मन्दिर निर्माण सम्पन्न भएपछि वज्रवाराहीको सुनको मूर्ति बनाउन लगाएका थिए । नेसं ७८६ चैत्र शुक्ल ८ (सन् १६६६) सोमवारको दिनमा विश्वनाथ उपाध्यायले वज्रवाराहीको सुनको मूर्ति विधिवत् रूपले प्रतिष्ठा गरेका थिए (Yogī Naraharinātha VS 2013, p. 58) ।भाषावंशावलीमा श्रीनिवास मल्लले मन्दिर निर्माण गरेको कुरा नलेखी वज्रवाराहीको मूर्ति स्थापना गरेको कुरा मात्र लेखिएको छ । उक्त वंशावलीअनुसार श्रीनिवास मल्लले बनाउन लगाएको वज्रवाराहीको सुनको मूर्ति नेसं ७८६ चैत्र शुक्ल ८ (सन् १६६६) मा सम्पन्न भएपछि नेसं ७८६ चैत्र शुक्ल ११ (सन् १६६६) मा विश्वनाथ उपाध्यायले पूजा गरी चापागाउँ परिक्रमा गराई विधिपूर्वक प्रतिष्ठा गरिदिएका थिए (D. Lamsāla VS 2023, p. 66) । नेसं ८२६ (सन् १७०६) मा पानी नपरेर दुःख भएकोले योगमती (राजा योगनरेन्द्र मल्लकी छोरी) र राजा लोकप्रकाश मल्ल (योगमतीका छोरा) ले मिलेर विभिन्न देवस्थलहरू पूजापाठ गरी पानी मागेका थिए । सोही क्रममा नेसं ८२६ (सन् १७०६) को असार महिनामा वज्रवाराहीकहाँ पानी माग्ने विधान पूरा गरिएको थियो (D. Lamsāla VS 2023, p. 74) ।अभिलेखीय प्रमाणको आधारमा हेर्दा उत्तरमध्यकालदेखि यस मन्दिरबारे सामग्रीहरू पाइन्छन् । नेसं ८१९ (सन् १६९९) मा चापागाउँ निवासी हेरनी मयीले वज्रवाराहीको लागि ८ रोपनी खेत गुठी राखिदिएकी थिइन् । नेसं ८२० (सन् १७००) मा राजा योगनरेन्द्र मल्लले वाद्यवादनसहित बलि दिई अहोरात्र यज्ञ गरी वज्रवाराहीदेवीको लागि मन्दिरअगाडि सुवर्ण छत्रसहित ढुङ्गाको राँगोको प्रतिमा चढाएका थिए । नेसं ८५५ (सन् १७३५) मा ललितपुरका राजा विष्णु मल्लले वज्रवाराही मन्दिर जीर्णोद्धार गरी सुवर्णकलश ध्वजारोहण गरेका थिए । यो मन्दिर गजूरबिनाको मन्दिर भनी प्रख्यात भएपनि विष्णु मल्लले जीर्णोद्धार गर्दा गजूर राखिएको थियो भन्ने कुरा यस अभिलेखले प्रमाणित गरेको छ । कालान्तरमा कुनै कारणले मन्दिरको पुनर्निर्माण गर्दा गजूर राख्न नसकिएपछि विभिन्न किम्बदन्तीहरू रचिएका हुनसक्छन् । विसं १९८७ (सन् १९३०) मा जीतगोविन्दले मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार गरेका थिए । विसं १९९० (सन् १९३४) को भूकम्पले मन्दिरलाई कुनै असर गरेन (Yogī Naraharinātha VS 2013, p. 58) । विसं २०१५ (सन् १९५९) मा राजा महेन्द्रले मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार गरेका थिए । विसं २०५७ (सन् २०००) मा मन्दिरका दुबै तहका छानाहरूमा तामाको पाता राखिएको थियो । विसं २०७२ (सन् २०१५) को भूकम्पले मन्दिरको पूर्वपट्टिको गारोमा क्षति पुगेको थियो । पुरातत्त्व विभागबाट प्राप्त रु. २० लाखको आर्थिक सहयोगबाट मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार गरिएको थियो (V. Karmācārya VS 2075, p.61) ।यस मन्दिरमा कर्माचार्य थरका पुजारीले नित्यपूजा गरिरहेका छन् । मन्दिरमा नित्यपूजा गर्न आयस्ताको लागि खेत र फूल चढाउनको लागि फूलबारीको व्यवस्था गरिएको थियो । गुठी संस्थानको लगतमा वज्रवाराहीको नित्यपूजाको लागि दुई रोपनी आठ आना जग्गा राखिएको देखिन्छ (Guṭhī Saṃsthāna VS 2071, p. 46) । तैपनि गुठी संस्थानबाट मन्दिरको नित्यपूजाको लागि कुनै सहयोग प्राप्त हुँदैन । बिहान नित्यपूजा र बेलुकी आरती हुँदाखेरी मन्दिरअगाडिको फल्चामा बसेर जुगीहरूले शहनाई बजाउँथे (V. Karmācārya VS 2075, p. 41), तर त्यसको लागि राखिएको जग्गा मासिएपछि शहनाई बजाउने कार्य पनि बन्द भइसकेको छ । मन्दिरका जग्गा मासिएपछि आर्थिक अभावको कारणले दशकौंसम्म नित्यपूजा बन्द भइसकेको थियो । विसं २०७९ (सन् २०२३) मा मन्दिर प्राङ्गणमा सप्ताहव्यापी महायज्ञ सञ्चालन गरेर सङ्कलन भएको रकमले अक्षयकोष खडा गरी नित्यपूजालाई पुनः निरन्तरता दिइएको छ । मन्दिरमा द्यःला जातिका मानिसहरूले द्यःपाःलाःको काम गर्दै आइरहेका छन् । द्यःलाःहरूका १२ वटा परिवारले १५-१५ दिनको पालो मिलाएर द्यःपाःलाःको काम गर्दै आइरहेका छन् ।प्रत्येक वर्ष चैत्र शुक्ल पूर्णिमा र कार्तिक शुक्ल ८ गरी वर्षको दुईपल्ट वज्रवाराहीको खटजात्रा सम्पन्न गरिन्छ । ती दुई खटजात्रमा खटमा राखेर जात्रा गर्नको लागि छुट्टछुट्टै वज्रवाराहीका मूर्तिहरू बनाइएका छन् । दुबै मूर्तिहरू भन्सार टोलमा रहेको वज्रवाराहीको द्यःछेँमा राखिएका हुन्छन् । नेसं ८१९ (सन् १६९९) को शिलापत्रमा दुबै खटजात्राको लागि खेत गुठी राखिदिएको प्रसङ्ग आएकोले त्यस मितिभन्दा पहिले नै दुबै जात्रा सञ्चालनमा आइसकेको कुरा पुष्टि हुन्छ ।प्रत्येक वर्ष चैत्र शुक्ल पूर्णिमाको खटजात्रालाई वज्रवाराहीको मूल जात्रा मानिन्छ । जात्राको क्रममा सिन्दूर पनि छरिने हुनाले यसलाई सिन्दूर जात्रा पनि भनिन्छ । यस जात्राको शुरुवातबारे एउटा किम्बदन्ती रहेको छ । भक्तपुरका राजा नरेन्द्रदेव युद्धको समापन पछि चापागाउँ हुँदै घर फर्कंदा निकै रात परेछ । उनले बाटोमा पर्ने देवीको घरमा बास माग्न सिपाहीलाई पठाएछन् । तर सिपाही डराएर राजा भएका ठाउँमा फर्केर "शिरदेखि पाउसम्म सेतो कपडाले छोपिएको डरलाग्दो आकृतिमा सुतिरहेको छ" भनी राजालाई सुनाएपछि राजा आफै हेर्न भनी गएछन् । राजाले पनि पूरै शरीर सेतो कपडाले छोपेर सुतिरहेको देखेपछि कपडा उघारेर हेर्दा वज्रवाराही माताको प्रत्यक्ष दर्शन पाएछन् । देवीले दर्शन दिएपछि "मेरो यस्तै मूर्ति बनाएर चैत्र पूर्णिमाको दिन जात्रा चलाउनू" भनी आदेश दिई अन्तर्ध्यान भएपछि त्यसै अनुसार मूर्ति र खट बनाएर जात्रा चलाइँदै आइरहेको छ (Dyaḥpāḥlāḥ of the temple from a Dyaḥlāḥ caste, female, age 58) । यस्तै खालको अर्को किम्बदन्तीमा राजाको नाम अरि मल्ल दिइएको छ (S. Mānandhara VS 2059, p. 62) ।विसं २०२५ (सन् १९६८) सालमा भन्सार टोलमा रहेको द्यःछेँमा राखिएको जात्रा गरिने वज्रवाराहीको मूर्ति चोरी भएको थियो (V. Karmācārya VS 2075, p. 38) । पछि त्रिभुवन विमानस्थलको झाडीमा फालिरहेको अवस्थामा भेटिएको थियो । मूर्तिलाई विदेश लैजान नसकेपछि विमानस्थलको झाडीमै फालिएको हुनसक्छ । मूर्तिको सुरक्षाको जिम्मा लिने भएमात्र चापागाउँमा फिर्ता गर्ने भनी सरकारी पक्षले शर्त राखेकोले कसैले पनि जिम्मा लिन मानेनन् । त्यसैले विसं २०२९ (सन् १९७२) सालदेखि उक्त मूर्तिलाई राष्ट्रिय सङ्ग्रहालयको संरक्षणमा राखिएको थियो । त्यसपछि जात्रा गर्नको लागि वज्रवाराहीको नयाँ मूर्ति बनाइएको थियो । उक्त नयाँ मूर्ति पनि चोरी भएको थियो जुन अहिलेसम्म पनि फेला परेको छैन । त्यसपछि पुनः अर्को मूर्ति बनाएर जात्रा गरिएको थियो । विसं २०७८ (सन् २०२१) सालमा राष्ट्रिय सङ्ग्रहालयमा राखिएको वज्रवाराहीको पुरानो मूर्ति चापागाउँमा फिर्ता ल्याइएको थियो । सम्पूर्ण कानूनी प्रक्रिया पूरा गरेर पुरातत्त्व विभागको निर्णयअनुसार गोदावरी नगरपालिकाका मेयर, उपमे​यर, जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय ललितपुरका प्रतिनिधि, पुरातत्त्व विभागका प्रतिनिधि र स्थानीय गुठीयारहरूको उपस्थितिमा राष्ट्रिय सङ्ग्रहालयका प्रमुखले गुठीलाई विधिवत् रूपले मूर्ति हस्तान्तरण गरेका थिए । अहिले वज्रवाराही द्यःछेँमा पुरानो वज्रवाराहीको मूर्ति र दोस्रोपल्ट चोरी भएपछि बनाइएको नयाँ मूर्ति गरी दुईवटा मूर्ति राखिएका छन् ।कार्तिक शुक्ल ८ मा गरिने खटजात्रालाई स्थानीयहरू 'मरस्ति जात्रा' भन्छन् । त्यस जात्रामा अष्टमातृकासहित सुनको जलप लगाइएको वज्रवाराहीको शिरलाई खटमा राखेर जात्रा गरिन्छ । अहिले यो जात्रा चापागाउँका देशारहरूले सञ्चालन गर्छन् । तर पहिले यो जात्रा बुलुका बासिन्दाहरूले सञ्चालन गर्थे । लोकधारणाअनुसार एकपल्ट बुलुका बासिन्दाहरूले जात्रा गर्न भनी वज्रवाराहीको मूर्ति ल्याएर मन्दिरभित्र स्थापना गरी विधिपूर्वक पूजा गरे । पूजापश्चात् देवीको मूर्तिको हेरचाह गर्न भनी एक बालिकालाई जिम्मा दिएर अरू मानिसहरू वनभोज खान गएका थिए । चापागाउँका देशार थरका युवाहरू आएर ती बालिकालाईभाभा काय्‌गु कि पापा(देवी मनपर्छ कि रोटी) भनी लोभ देखाए । भोकाएकी ती बालिकाले रोटी लिने भनेपछि उसलाई रोटी दिई वज्रवाराहीको मूर्तिलाई चापागाउँका देशारहरूले कब्जा गरी गाउँभरि परिक्रमा गरी जात्रा गरेका थिए (Pradhan 1981, p. 8) । जात्रा संचालन गर्ने अधिकार खोसिएपनि जात्रामा बुलुवासीको सक्रिय सहभागिता अहिलेसम्म पनि देखिन्छ । विसं २०४२-२०४३ (सन् १९८५-१९८६) तिर जात्रा गरिने वज्रवाराहीको शिरको प्रतिमा चोरी भएकोले लामो समयसम्म यो जात्रा बन्द भएको थियो । विसं २०७९ (सन् २०२२) मा नयाँ मूर्ति बनाएर पुनः जात्रा सञ्चालन गरिएको थियो (A Local resident from a Deśāra caste, male, age 44) ।* यो मन्दिर शुरुदेखि गजूरविहीन थिएन । नेसं ८५५ (सन् १७३५) मा राजा विष्णु मल्लले मन्दिर जीर्णोद्धार गर्दा सुनको गजूर चढाएको अभिलेखीय प्रमाण भेट्टिएको छ । हेर्नू - CHG0110_I_004
references: Sources and references Sources Stone inscription from NS 819 stored inside a phalcā on the west side of the temple. H: 55 cm, W: 26 cm, D: 7 cm. D. Vajrācārya VS 2056, pp. 317-318; S. Mānandhara VS 2059, pp. 80-81.

historical_events.event_description: Heranī Mayī, a resident of the Pasiṃkochẽ Ṭola northeast of Cāpāgāũ, established a religious trust by donating eightropanīs of land to Vajravārāhī. The income from the land was designated for donating various items, including puffed rice, beaten rice, curd, meat, and fermented beer, during the processions in Caitra and Kārtika. Lamps were also to be lit on these occasions. The trust was further obligated to annually feedjogis and make special offerings to them on the new moon day of Bhadra.

historical_events.event_name: Installation of a stone buffalo statue
historical_events.event_description: King Yoganarendra Malla installed a stone buffalo statue with a golden parasol at the temple after performing a night-long fire sacrifice with music and offerings.

historical_events.event_name: Offering of a pair of lions (CHG0110-035, CHG0110-036)
historical_events.event_description: A pair of stone lion statues (CHG0110-035, CHG0110-036) were installed on either side of the passage to the temple complex. The name of the donor is not mentioned in the inscription.

King Viṣṇu Malla of Lalitpur renovated the Vajravārāhī temple and organized the ‘suvarṇakalaśadhvajārohaṇa’ceremony, involving the installation of a golden finial and the hoisting of a banner. Priests and astrologers like Viśvānanda and Nīlakaṇṭhānanda participated in the ritual. The inscription records the king's donation of land to commemorate the anniversary of the finial installation and mandates annual fire rituals with animal sacrifice. This inscription contradicts the popular belief that the temple has never had a finial.

historical_events.event_name: Endowment of lands to repair a phalcā
historical_events.event_description: Gaṃgāsāgara Bābu of the Bhansāra Ṭola in Cāpāgāũ, along with his wife Rājalakṣmī, renovated aphalcaand established a religious trust by donating land. The income from this land was to be used for repairing thephalca's roof and making ancestral offerings in the name of his uncle Mastarāma on the 3rd of the dark fortnight of Phālguna, prior to the worship at the Vajravārāhī temple. It remains unclear which of the threephalcās—west, north, or south of the temple—was renovated.

During the reign of King Surendra, Kāyaṣṭha Akabara Bhāro of the Bhansāra Ṭola in Cāpāgāũ established a religious trust by donating land for cleaning the temple premises daily. He made the donation together with his mother Guṇa Thaku and his sons Mānakāji, Kṛṣṇamehera, Syāmamehera, and Rāmamehera, wishing for the deliverance of his ancestors. He also mandated an annual worship of Vajravārāhī on the 8th of the bright fortnight of Caitra, followed by a feast.
Balabhadra Kāri Kṣitri installed a bell (CHG0110-007) at the temple.
Bahādura Kāki Kṣetṛ renovated and reinstalled the bell (CHG0110-007) offered to the temple by his father Balabhadra Kāri Kṣitri.

Together with his wife Devi Thaku and the family members, Kāyaṣṭha Akabara Bhāro of the Bhansāra Ṭola in Cāpāgāũ installed a brass toraṇa above the entrance to the temple. He also overlaid the entrance with brass sheets on the occasion.
An ascetic named Kāśi Girī established aśivaliṅga(CHG0110-025) north of the temple and named it Kāśī Viśveśvara Mahādeva.

historical_events.event_name: Offering of silver toraṇa, serpent noose, and parasol
historical_events.event_description: Kālu Siṃ offered Vajravārāhī a silvertoraṇa(decorative arch), anāgapāśa(serpent noose), and a parasol, with a combined weight of 221tolās of silver. He also presented a 15-tolāsilver garland to the buffalo figure (CHG0110-024), Vajravārāhī's animal mount. These offerings were to be displayed during festivals and on Saturdays. The donor further stipulated that Vajravārāhī be worshipped with an animal sacrifice on the 3rd of the dark fortnight of Jyeṣṭha, the day his father, Harṣanarasiṃha, passed away. He established a trust with land donation to ensure the continuation of these practices.

historical_events.event_name: Offering of a pair of flags
historical_events.event_description: Haribhakta, Caityalakṣmī, and others from Dau Bāhāḥ in Patan installed a pair of brass banners flanking the entrance to the temple.

Together with his sons Kīrtigovinda and Pūrṇagovinda, Jītagovinda Amātya from Dau Bāhāḥ in Patan installed two pairs of stone lion statues in front of the northern (CHG0110-009, CHG0110-010) and southern entrances (CHG0110-011, CHG0110-012) of the temple.

historical_events.event_name: Repair of the temple and offering of a bell (CHG0110-021)
historical_events.event_description: Jītagovinda renovated the temple and offered a bell (CHG0110-021). He probably is the same person who installed two pairs of lion statues in front of the northern and southern entrances of the temple.
A stonemaṇḍalawas (CHG0110-022) by the wife of Candramāna from the Ikhā Ṭola in Cāpāgāũ.
King Mahendra renovated the temple and built walls around the temple premises.
Bhairavabahādura Śreṣṭha and Candramehara Kāyaṣṭha jointly renovated and reinstalled the bell (CHG0110-021) previously offered by Jītagovinda.
During the reign of King Virendra, both roofs of the temple were laid with copper sheets.

The upper roof of the Vajravārāhī temple was covered with zinc sheets, while the lower roof was covered with tiles. Due to the deterioration of both roofs, leading to leaks and rotting of the wooden rafters, financial assistance was collected from various sources to replace both roofs with copper sheets. A marble inscription was installed to commemorate this event.
Śānti KC from Jharuvārāsī offered a bell (CHG0110-014) in memory of her decease husband Pūrṇabahādura KC.
Together with their sons, Herālāla and Dāntīmāyā Maharjana of Thecva offered an oblong banner (patāḥ) of copper to the temple.

In memory of her husband, Bhairavabahādura Jośī, Miśrī Jośī and her family members constructed a section of the southern boundary wall of the temple premises, extending from the door on the wall to the southwestern corner.
Residents of Saugal in Patan, Puruṣottamabahādura Śreṣṭha and his wife Maiyā Śreṣṭha installed a metalmaṇḍala(CHG0110-016) in the temple premises.
Kṛṣṇabahādura Sāhī and Tulsīmāyā Sāhī from Jhyālipāṭī in Cāpāgāũ established a Gaṇeśa statue in the temple premises.

Dāna Darśana and his family installed temple bells on the eaves of the upper roof of the temple in the name of his decease parents Śrīnātha and Santamāyā Darśana. He also established statues of his parents.
Amara Rājabhaṇḍārī and his wife Tārādevī Rājabhaṇḍārī installed a woodentoraṇaover the eastern entrance of the temple.

Along with his family, Puruṣottamabahādura Śreṣṭha of Saugal, Patan established new statues of theaṣṭamātṛkādeities inside the sanctum after the previous ones were worn out. He established these statues in the name of his deceased family members Mānabahādura, Gaṇeśakumārī, Śambhūbahādura, and Pūrṇakumārī Śreṣṭha.
Along with his wife Dātīmāyā Maharjana and the family, Harikṛṣṇa Maharjana of Cāpāgāũ offered a silver crown to the goddess.

Jayakṛṣṇa Bhāro, Devidāsa Bhāro, and others jointly offered a woodentoraṇaover the southern entrance of the temple. While the inscription does not contain a date, the donation appears to have taken place in later-medieval period.
Kṛṣṇabahādura Maharjana of Thecva offered an oblong banner (patāḥ) to the temple in the name of his deceased wife Lakṣmīkumārī Maharjana.
An oblong banner (patāḥ) was offered to the temple in the name of the donor’s deceased parents Siddhilāla and Harṣamāyā. The inscription does not mention the name of the donor.
